planting.note: Divide corm chains in early spring before growth resumes, or plant container specimens in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Lucifer is a Crocosmia masoniorum hybrid and one of the most widely grown named crocosmia cultivars, valued for its exceptionally vivid, large, blazing-red flowers and strong garden vigor.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Lucifer is arguably the most famous named crocosmia cultivar, a Crocosmia masoniorum hybrid bred by British plantsman Alan Bloom and prized for its extraordinarily vivid, saturated red flowers held in arching, one-sided sprays above bold, pleated, sword-like foliage in mid to late summer. It is among the hardiest and most vigorous crocosmia cultivars available, tolerating colder winters than many other crocosmia and multiplying readily by corm offsets into substantial clumps within a few years. The intensely red, tubular flowers are a magnet for hummingbirds and make excellent, long-lasting cut flowers. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring, since crowded corms produce progressively fewer and shorter flower spikes over time. In colder parts of its range, mulch heavily over the corms for winter protection; in zone 8–9 it is reliably hardy in the ground year-round. Give it full sun to light afternoon shade and consistently moist, well-drained soil for the best flower display.
